questions.question: What should a player be able to say about this game in one sentence?
questions.why: A short pitch keeps the plan focused.

questions.question: What does a player do during their first thirty seconds?
questions.why: The first action teaches the main loop.

questions.question: Who would choose to play this, and for how long at a time?
questions.why: This helps choose session length and difficulty.

exit_criteria: Write the pitch, audience and what makes play worth repeating.

questions.question: What action does the player repeat, and what changes after each attempt?
questions.why: It defines what the player learns.

questions.question: How does a round end, and what happens when the player loses?
questions.why: A clear restart makes failure understandable.

questions.question: What unlocks or gets harder as the player improves?
questions.why: Progress should have a visible signal.

exit_criteria: Describe a complete loop from player action to feedback, reward and next action.

questions.question: Which art and sounds do you already own or have permission to use?
questions.why: The team needs a lawful source for each asset.

questions.question: What is the oldest device you want the game to run well on?
questions.why: Performance targets need a device to test.

questions.question: What should survive when the player closes the game or changes devices?
questions.why: That decides what to describe in SAVE_DATA.

exit_criteria: Identify asset sources, target devices and a usable substitute for anything missing.

questions.question: What is the smallest complete match or level you could test?
questions.why: A short slice proves the loop early.

questions.question: How will you tell that a round is too hard or slow?
questions.why: A measure makes the first balance pass repeatable.

questions.question: Which three numbers should you be able to change between playtests?
questions.why: Named controls make balance adjustments safe.

exit_criteria: List tunable values, playtest measures and one smallest playable slice.

release_check.procedure: Install or extract the release build in a clean supported environment. Launch it and capture one successful playable flow.
